title: Affineness from a faithful rational action fixing a point
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed subgroups as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Dimensions mean topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected separated finite-type $k$-group scheme and let $X$ be an integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $Y\subseteq X$ be a nonempty dense open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] with a regular action $a:G\times_kY\to Y$, meaning a morphism satisfying the unit and multiplication identities; products are scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume this action is faithful: the only closed subgroup scheme $K\hookrightarrow G$ whose restricted action on $Y$ is the second projection, after every base change by a commutative $k$-algebra, is the identity subgroup. Let $\alpha:G\times_kX\dashrightarrow X$ be the rational extension of $a$, where a rational map is an equivalence class of morphisms on dense open subschemes, with its largest domain of definition. Suppose that $P\in X(k)$, that $\alpha$ is defined at $(e,P)$, and that the restriction to $V\times_k\{P\}$ is the constant morphism with value $P$, where $V=\{g:(g,P)\in\operatorname{Dom}(\alpha)\}$. Then $G$ is affine, meaning isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative $k$-algebra [def-pc-scheme]. No global regular action on $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, p.150 (faithful fixed-point action and finite jets), and Proposition 8.25, p.154 (rational-action variant). The variant is used explicitly in the last paragraph of the proof of Proposition 4.1 in Milne (2013), p.9, referring to its Proposition 2.6; local article WANTED, read arXiv:1311.6060v2 online. No Stacks tag states this rational fixed-point criterion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-rational-fixed-section-jets] to $G,X,Y,a,\alpha,P$. It applies without smoothness of $X$ or a global action on $X$. Thus $D=\operatorname{Dom}(\alpha)$ contains the entire fixed section $G\times\{P\}$, and there are compatible inverse-pullback representations $\rho_n$ on the nonzero finite-dimensional algebras $Q_n$ with descending closed finite-type subgroup kernels $K_n$.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, printed p.150, construction of the jet representations; Proposition 8.25, printed p.154, rational-action variant. Agent-extracted local-action input, not the global-action assertion of Proposition 8.9. The missing detailed local argument is written in report.md. The rational variant is explicitly used in Milne (2013), Proposition 4.1, final paragraph, arXiv:1311.6060v2 (local article WANTED). No Stacks tag states this local-action construction.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$) and its spectrum is quasi-compact. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $G$ Noetherian. Choose a finite affine cover with Noetherian coordinate rings, using [pqf-def-locnoeth]. On each chart, the closed immersions $K_n\hookrightarrow G$ correspond to ideals $I_n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion]. They form an increasing chain. Its union is an ideal, finitely generated by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; all generators lie in a single $I_N$, so the chain stabilizes. Taking the maximum of the finitely many chart bounds gives $K_n=K_N=:K$ for all $n\geq N$.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, p.150, stabilization of the descending kernels; affine-ideal expansion. Stacks Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01OV (definition-noetherian), 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion).

proof.text: For every $n\geq N$ the representation $\rho_n|_K$ is the identity by the definition of kernel. Compatibility also makes $\rho_n|_K$ the identity for $1\leq n<N$. Consequently the action of $K$ on every $X_n$ is trivial: inverse pullback is the identity, hence so is direct pullback. Set $E=D\times_GK\subseteq K\times X$. It contains $K\times\{P\}$ and $K\times Y$. Apply [lem-sfb-constant-family-jet-equality] with $T=K$, $Z=X$, and the two morphisms $\alpha|_E,p_X|_E$. Its hypotheses hold: $K$ is finite type, $X$ is integral separated, and the two maps agree on every $K\times X_n$. They therefore agree on $E$, in particular on $K\times Y$. This is equality of morphisms, so remains true after every algebra base change. The assumed faithfulness on $Y$ forces the closed subgroup $K$ to be the identity subgroup.

source.place: Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module), especially (1) and its proof by local Krull intersection. Agent-formulated constant-family morphism-detection consequence, with its argument recorded in report.md; this geometric statement is not itself the Stacks lemma. It isolates the formal-detection input in Milne, Algebraic Groups, Proposition 8.9, printed p.150, for the rational-action argument of Proposition 8.25.

proof.text: The map $\rho_N$ is injective on every algebra's points: if $\rho_N(g)=\rho_N(h)$, then $h^{-1}g\in K_N=1$, so $g=h$. Choose a basis of $Q_N$, of dimension $d\geq1$. The group $\operatorname{GL}_d$ is the affine separated finite-type group [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Since $G$ is also separated finite type, [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-monomorphism-closed-immersion] makes $\rho_N:G\to\operatorname{GL}_d$ a closed immersion. Apply (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] to the affine open equal to all of $\operatorname{GL}_d$: its inverse image is $G$, which is affine as required.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, p.150, last sentence; Theorem 5.34, pp.106--107; Stacks Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion).

split_report.summary: Separated the rational fixed-section jet construction from formal detection over nonreduced parameter schemes. Stabilized kernels scheme-theoretically by affine ideal chains, applied faithfulness on Y only after equality of morphisms, and used the existing monomorphism criterion to conclude affineness. Preserved all hypotheses and repaired doubled TeX escapes. The existing smooth global-action jet node does not apply.

The route was checked against Milne iAG2017 Prop 8.9 (p.150; the errata's 'X reduced' holds because X is integral here) and Prop 8.25 (p.154). The split follows 8.9 step for step: new node rational-fixed-section-jets builds the jets ρ_n and the kernels K_n; step 2 shows the kernels stabilise through Noetherian affine charts; step 3 replaces X^H by the equalizer and uses new node constant-family-jet-equality (Krull intersection, coherence, and schematic density from Ass of the flat family T×X→T) to get a|_{K×Y}=pr, so faithfulness gives K=1; step 4 uses the monomorphism node to get a closed immersion into GL_d (d≥1) and then the 01QO criterion (1) to make G affine. Both new statements are true. I proved each myself: the domain extension via α(gv,α(v⁻¹,x)), the jets factoring because α is scheme-theoretically constant on the reduced G×P, and jet-equality tested with T=Spec k[ε], X=A¹. Neither new node restates a clause of the item, and they are of comparable size. Duplicate search over the whole DAG found nothing; fixed-point-action-finite-jets needs a global action and smooth X, and dense-fixed-local-ideal-jets needs G affine. Batch-5 flag: the closure of monomorphism-closed-immersion reaches def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space through trivial-kernel-homogeneous-quotient; that is the general definition of a scheme as an algebraic space and the other trf nodes reached are generic foundations, not steps of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so accepted. No cycle, no tool_uses needed, no SGA. Minor: the citations.json the report mentions is not in the commit. No changes made.

lean.statement: theorem isAffine_of_rational_fixed_point {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (G X Y : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] [Smooth G.hom] [ConnectedSpace G.left] [IsSeparated G.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] [IsIntegral X.left] [IsSeparated X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom] (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j.left] [Nonempty Y.left] (hdense : Dense (Set.range j.left)) [ModObj G Y] (hfaithful : ∀ (K : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj K] (i : K ⟶ G) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme i], (i ⊗ₘ 𝟙 Y) ≫ ModObj.smul (M := G) (X := Y) = snd K Y → i = toUnit K ≫ η[G]) (α : (G ⊗ X).left.PartialMap X.left) (hmax : α.domain = α.toRationalMap.domain) (hextends : ∃ t : (G ⊗ Y).left ⟶ α.domain.toScheme, t ≫ α.domain.ι = (𝟙 G ⊗ₘ j).left ∧ t ≫ α.hom = (ModObj.smul (M := G) (X := Y) ≫ j).left) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ X) (hdefined : ∃ p : (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))).left ⟶ α.domain.toScheme, p ≫ α.domain.ι = (lift η[G] P).left) (hfixed : ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (g : T ⟶ G) (d : T.left ⟶ α.domain.toScheme), d ≫ α.domain.ι = (lift g (toUnit T ≫ P)).left → d ≫ α.hom = (toUnit T ≫ P).left) : IsAffine G.left
